# Provider Portability v1.0.0 — Where We Are

**Date:** 2026-05-15 (end of this push)
**Branch:** `spec/provider-portability`
**Last commit on top of main + 30:** `95ce8748` (Phase 5b.5.a — StaticCatalogProvider)

---

## The one-paragraph summary

v1.0.0 has the bones in place. The substrate exists, two adapters work, the framework + model fitness catalog is researched and locked, the user-facing UX layer is built and unit-tested, and the cost-aware routing math is locked. **What we don't have yet is end-to-end exercise of the whole thing as a system.** Unit tests are deep but they're each scoped to a single component. Production wiring of the new pieces into the running server hasn't happened. Real-API integration confirmation only exists for two of the touch points (Phase 4 Codex spawn fix, the canary signal). The next phase of work is end-to-end stitching plus the verification gates to catch the kind of drift that unit tests can't see.

---

## What's done

| Phase | What it is | State |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Substrate primitives (51 capabilities) | Locked, in src/providers/primitives/ |
| **2** | Capability registry, routing interface, conformance shells | Built; conformance suites are still no-op stubs (see gap below) |
| **3** | Anthropic adapters — headless (SDK credit path) + interactive-pool (subscription path) | Built. Real-API verified for the canary signal. Not yet exercised against the new router. |
| **4** | OpenAI Codex adapter | Built. Real-API verified end-to-end (Phase 4 smoke test passes). |
| **5a** | Model + framework fitness catalogs | Researched (Nate B Jones + Chinese open-source frontier), structured, locked. Hand-curated runtime view shipped today as the StaticCatalogProvider. |
| **5b spec** | Suggest-and-confirm UX design | Locked 2026-05-15 with your four answers (Telegram-only, sticky-yes-with-note, three re-ask triggers, override-via-slash-or-phrasing). ELI16 companion shipped. |
| **5b implementation (structural)** | All seven components: PreferenceStore, TriggerGate, TaskClassifier, OverrideDetector, TelegramConfirmer, FrameworkModelRouter, StaticCatalogProvider | All built. 115 unit tests cover every flow path. Each component is independently fail-safe (errors collapse to "ask the user" or "use the catalog default", never to a wrong silent answer). |
| **5c** | Cost-aware routing math | Built. 23 unit tests cover the six-row decision matrix and the three material-shift categories. |

---

## What's tested well

- **Per-component logic.** Every Phase 5b/5c component has its own unit test file and covers every branch.
- **Failure modes within a component.** Every "LLM throws," "provider returns null," "timeout fires," "config invalid" path returns the safe outcome.
- **The Anthropic interactive-pool canary.** The empty-prompt drift detector has its own canary, its own self-healing path, its own scheduled recurrence, and an LLM fallback for last-line-of-defense. That whole loop has been real-API exercised.
- **OpenAI Codex spawn loop.** Real-API verified after the stdin-hang fix.

---

## Two coverage gaps you raised after the first draft

These were not in my original report. They are real gaps. Honest current state below, sourced from a direct audit of the codebase rather than memory.

### Gap A — Claude-specific identity files (CLAUDE.md vs AGENT.md)

**Where we are right now:**
- AGENT.md exists as a framework-agnostic identity file. Init scaffolding generates it. Several core modules (TemporalCoherenceChecker, ContextSnapshotBuilder, ScopeVerifier) already read AGENT.md by default.
- CLAUDE.md still exists as the Claude Code-specific instructions file. Init scaffolds BOTH because Claude Code auto-loads CLAUDE.md from the project root at session start — that's a Claude Code convention we can't break for Claude users.
- The ProjectMapper checks both in this order: CLAUDE.md first, then AGENT.md fallback. That's Claude-first lookup that needs to flip or become provider-aware.
- About eight to ten places still hard-code the CLAUDE.md path (PostUpdateMigrator, ScopeCoherenceTracker, a few command files). These are Claude-only patches that won't apply for non-Claude installs.
- Zero awareness of Codex's equivalent convention (AGENTS.md per OpenAI), Gemini's, or anything else.

**What needs to happen for v1.0.0:**
1. Decide the canonical identity file. My recommendation: AGENT.md is the canonical instar source-of-truth. CLAUDE.md (and AGENTS.md for Codex, and any others) become rendered VIEWS of AGENT.md — written at scaffold time and re-rendered when AGENT.md changes. The agent's "identity" lives in one place; each framework gets the file it expects in the shape it expects.
2. Flip the lookup priority: AGENT.md primary, CLAUDE.md fallback (the reverse of today).
3. Add a render step at init / update time that writes the framework-specific shadow files from the canonical AGENT.md.
4. Remove the eight-to-ten hardcoded CLAUDE.md references in favor of the canonical lookup.

**How we test it:**
- Unit test for the renderer: given an AGENT.md, asserts CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md outputs match expected templates.
- Round-trip test: scaffold a fresh agent with framework=codex, verify only AGENTS.md is generated (not CLAUDE.md). Same with framework=claude (only CLAUDE.md gets the shadow). With framework=both, both shadows generated.
- Migration test: existing agent with CLAUDE.md gets migrated correctly when AGENT.md doesn't exist yet.

### Gap B — Jobs and sentinels across providers

**Where we are right now:** the picture is mixed. The audit categorizes each sentinel:

| Component | Lock-in | What's wrong |
|---|---|---|
| CommitmentSentinel | clean | provider-agnostic via IntelligenceProvider |
| MessageSentinel | clean | provider-agnostic |
| CoherenceMonitor | clean | generic health check |
| LifelineHealthWatchdog | clean | generic process health |
| SessionActivitySentinel | partial | requires tmux session name for output capture |
| SessionWatchdog | partial | tmux-specific kill escalation logic |
| CompactionSentinel | partial | assumes ~/.claude/projects/<hash> session path |
| HelperWatchdog | partial | hardcoded anthropic-error regex |
| delivery-failure-sentinel | partial | depends on Threadline relay (Anthropic-specific) |

**Plus three hard locks at the runtime layer:**
- `detectClaudePath()` in Config.ts throws an error if the `claude` binary isn't found. This blocks every non-Claude install today.
- Five files reference `claudePath` directly (Config, ClaudeCliIntelligenceProvider, Prerequisites, SessionManager, types).
- The only IntelligenceProvider implementation is ClaudeCliIntelligenceProvider — every reviewer / sentinel / canary that goes through IntelligenceProvider runs through `claude -p` today.

**What needs to happen for v1.0.0:**
1. Generalize `detectClaudePath()` into a `detectProviderBinary(provider)` that picks the right binary for the configured framework (claude, codex, etc.).
2. Build the second IntelligenceProvider implementation — likely `CodexCliIntelligenceProvider` — so the reviewer / sentinel / canary loops can run through Codex when the agent's framework is set to Codex.
3. Replace the tmux-specific session output capture with a transport-aware shim. SessionManager already abstracts session lifecycle; the capture path needs the same treatment.
4. Replace hardcoded `anthropic-error` regex in HelperWatchdog with a provider-driven failure-pattern table that each adapter contributes.
5. Decide what happens to Threadline relay — keep it Anthropic-only, or extend? My recommendation: keep it Anthropic-only for v1.0.0, document the limitation, plan extension as post-v1.0.0 work.

**How we test it:**
- Per-sentinel matrix test: spin up each sentinel against a stub framework=codex setup, assert it doesn't reach for Claude-only code paths. Currently zero of these tests exist.
- Boot test: start instar with `INSTAR_FRAMEWORK=codex` and no Claude binary installed. Today this throws at startup; after the fix it should boot cleanly.
- End-to-end sentinel test: trigger a known stall in a Codex-routed session, verify the StallTriage path fires correctly (not the Anthropic-error regex path).

### How these two gaps slot into the v1.0.0 plan

Both belong in Phase 7 (migration design + local agent testing) plus a new Phase 5e (framework-binary abstraction). I'd add to the proposed order:

- After 5b.5.c (server composition root) and before 5b.5.d (real Telegram test): **Phase 5e — generalize the runtime binary abstraction.** Without this, end-to-end Codex routing literally cannot work because the IntelligenceProvider implementation is Claude-only.
- After Phase 6 spec and before Phase 7 migration: **Phase 6.5 — generalize the identity-file rendering.** The canonical-AGENT.md + framework-shadow approach.

These additions probably add 3-4 days to the v1.0.0 critical path but they're load-bearing for the "supports any framework" promise of v1.0.0. Without them, v1.0.0 has multi-provider routing on paper but still requires Claude installed locally.

---

## What's tested badly or not at all

These are the gaps that worry me when I think about robustness for v1.0.0:

### 1. End-to-end task lifecycle
**No test exists** that runs a real task through: classify → look up preference → maybe ask via Telegram → pick framework+model → route to adapter via cost-aware policy → adapter runs → response comes back. Every piece has been tested alone, but the chain has never been pulled end-to-end. Even with all green unit tests, the integration is unverified.

### 2. The Telegram round-trip
The TelegramConfirmer is built and tested against a stub transport. The real bridge — pulling user replies out of the existing Telegram message stream onto the "await next reply on this topic" contract — has not been written. Until that exists, Phase 5b cannot actually ask you anything.

### 3. The conformance suites
Phase 2 declared 51 conformance suites (one per primitive) so every adapter could prove it honors the contract. Only ONE of those 51 has actual behavior assertions (OneShotCompletion). The other 50 are no-op stubs that call a getAssertions() helper that returns no-op stubs. Running the conformance suite right now passes 51/51 — but verifies zero behaviors. This is the single biggest false-confidence trap in the codebase.

### 4. Real cost-state plumbing
The cost-aware router takes a function that returns the current SDK credit pot state. No production wiring exists yet that connects that function to the Anthropic OAuth usage API. Today's behavior with no wiring is "treat state as unknown → conservatively use subscription path," which is safe but means the prepaid pot doesn't actually get drained as designed.

### 5. Migration path
We haven't tested how an existing instar agent (Echo, Inspec, etc.) migrates from "everything goes through claude code directly" to "everything goes through the new routing layer." Schema migrations for the preference store, config updates, breakage modes during upgrade — all unverified.

### 6. Cross-provider failure recovery
When the cost-aware router falls back from SDK-credit path to subscription path mid-stream (e.g., a 429 comes back during a long run), what actually happens? The decision is correct on paper, but the recovery flow hasn't been exercised.

### 7. The CoherenceReviewer test rewrite (smaller)
69 tests in that file have been broken since the Rule 2 cleanup because they were built on a fetch-mock pattern that no longer exists. Tracked but not yet fixed. Low priority for v1.0.0 but adds noise to the test summary.

---

## What I'd recommend (in priority order)

Each "phase" here is roughly one autonomous session.

### Order proposal

1. **5b.5.b — TelegramConfirmationTransport.** Bridge the existing Telegram adapter onto the ConfirmationTransport interface the confirmer expects. Unit-testable against a stub Telegram bot. Unlocks 5b.5.c.

2. **5b.5.c — Server.ts composition root.** Construct the FrameworkModelRouter at startup, expose it where messages enter the system, hook the cost-state tracker to the live Anthropic usage API. After this, the whole Phase 5b loop is live.

3. **5b.5.d — Real Telegram round-trip integration test.** One test, real bot, real LLM (fast tier). Sends you a confirmation prompt, you reply, we assert the preference cache updated and the right adapter ran. Probably the single highest-leverage test for v1.0.0 confidence.

4. **End-to-end test harness.** A new tests/e2e/ file that exercises classify → route → adapter → response for each of: Anthropic SDK-credit path, Anthropic subscription path, OpenAI Codex path. Real APIs. ONE happy-path test per stack, plus one failure-recovery test (intentional 429 / quota exhaust).

5. **Conformance suite rollout.** Replace the 50 no-op stubs with real behavior assertions following the OneShotCompletion template. Multi-day; spec compliance hard gate before v1.0.0 ships.

6. **Phase 5d (benchmarking) spec.** Not implementation — just the locked design for how the catalog stays honest over time. Implementation lands after v1.0.0.

7. **Phase 6 (OSS adapter) spec.** Same — design only, lock the integration points so v1.0.0 doesn't paint us into a corner.

8. **Phase 7 — migration design.** How existing agents move to the new substrate. Spec + a verified migration of Echo as the canary install.

9. **Phase 8 — v1.0.0 release.** Final release notes, version bump, npm publish, post-release verification.

### Critical-path estimate
If we go in this order, items 1-4 are the must-have-before-shipping core. 5 is the spec-compliance gate. 6-9 are wrap-up. Realistic timing: 1-2 weeks of focused work depending on how much real-API debugging surfaces.

---

## Decisions I need from you

**1. Testing-bar acceptance** — for end-to-end tests, do you want:
- **(a)** Real APIs every run (slow + costs money but high-confidence) — implies a CI budget cap
- **(b)** Real APIs gated behind an env flag (default mocked, INSTAR_REAL_API=1 to run real) — what we do for the Codex smoke test today
- **(c)** Real APIs once per phase exit and mocked otherwise — verified-at-merge-then-mocked-day-to-day

My recommendation: **(b)** — keeps day-to-day CI fast, makes the real-API path explicitly opt-in for release-gate runs. Mirrors the existing INSTAR_REAL_API pattern.

**2. Phase 5d / Phase 6 / Phase 7 — spec OR full implementation before v1.0.0?**
My recommendation: **spec only** for 5d and 6 (benchmarking + OSS adapter design locked, implementation post-v1.0.0). **Full implementation** for 7 (migration is required because v1.0.0 ships to existing installs).

**3. Multi-agent rollout** — for Phase 7, do we migrate just Echo, or also Inspec, or every agent on your machine?
My recommendation: **Echo first as the canary**, run for 24-48 hours, then roll the rest. Echo is the developer agent so I'm the canary install — failures get caught and fixed faster than on a passive agent.

**4. Cost cap for real-API testing** — what's the budget for running E2E tests through Claude + Codex real APIs?
My recommendation: **$5 per full E2E run, $50/month aggregate** — generous enough for active iteration, capped enough that a runaway test loop can't drain real money. Implement as a hard pre-run check that calls the existing UsageMeterProvider and refuses to start if remaining budget < $5.

---

## What I do NOT need from you

To keep momentum:
- I can pick the conformance-suite assertion shape per primitive without asking. The template exists.
- I can write the Phase 5d / 6 specs autonomously and ship them for your review at convergence time.
- I can build 5b.5.b/c against deterministic stubs and only ping you when the live Telegram round-trip test is ready to run against your actual phone.

Items I'll surface back: the four decisions above, the live-Telegram test moment (so we time it together), and any phase-exit acceptance failures.
